title: Cardinal DriveSense One-Enrollment-per-Vehicle Rule and Re-Enrollment Waiting Period
content:
## Rule

Cardinal DriveSense is held per vehicle. A vehicle may have only one enrollment that is enrolled, observing or scored, and a customer may enroll every scheduled vehicle, with no cap of its own. A vehicle can be enrolled only when it has no enrollment that is enrolled, observing or scored, and not within the re-enrollment waiting period after its last opt-out or termination.

## Program figures

| Program | Enrollments allowed per vehicle that are enrolled, observing or scored | Re-enrollment waiting period after an opt-out or termination (calendar days) |
|---|---|---|
| Cardinal DriveSense Mobile | 1 | 90 |
| Cardinal DriveSense Plug-In | 1 | 90 |
| Cardinal DriveSense Connected Car | 1 | 90 |
| Cardinal DriveSense Teen Coach | 1 | 90 |
| Cardinal DriveSense Miles Mobile | 1 | 180 |
| Cardinal DriveSense Miles Plug-In | 1 | 180 |

There is no per-customer limit: the number of enrolled vehicles a customer may hold is capped only by the number of vehicles scheduled, one enrollment each.

## What decides it

The decision rests on the company's own DriveSense enrollment records for **that vehicle**, read before the enrollment is made — not on the customer's account of them:

- the status of each enrollment on the vehicle (enrolled, observing, scored, opted out or terminated); and
- for an enrollment that has ended, its end date (the date of the opt-out, or the date the enrollment ended).

Enrollments held on the customer's other vehicles do not bear on this vehicle.

## Decision table

| The vehicle has an enrollment that is enrolled, observing or scored | The vehicle is within the waiting period after its last opt-out or termination | The vehicle can be enrolled |
|---|---|---|
| Yes | — | No |
| No | Yes | No |
| No | No | Yes |

## Illustrations (hypothetical vehicles)

1. A vehicle whose enrollment shows observing cannot take a second enrollment, on the same program or another.
2. A vehicle whose only enrollment shows opted out, with an end date 40 days ago, is within the waiting period (40 days is inside both 90 and 180) and cannot be enrolled yet.
3. A vehicle whose only enrollment shows terminated, with an end date 200 days ago, is outside the waiting period (200 days is beyond both 90 and 180) and has no enrollment that is enrolled, observing or scored, so it can be enrolled.
4. A customer with three scheduled vehicles, none with an enrollment on file, may enroll all three, one enrollment per vehicle.
